newsitem.title: USA: American Airlines reports $284 million profit.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines reports $284 million profit.

text.p: American Airlines parent AMR Corp. reported $284 million in fourth-quarter profits Wednesday amid a robust recovery in the airline industry.

The profits, equal to $3.08 a share, compared with a loss of $282 million, or $3.69 a share, in the fourth quarter of 1995 for the Fort Worth, Texas-based airline, and included several extraordinary items.
Revenues rose 3 percent to $4.33 billion from $4.19 billion a year earlier.
"We had quite a successful fourth quarter, which rounded out a very satisfactory year," AMR Chairman Robert Crandall said in a statement.
AMR stock was up $1.75 at $85.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.

American, the nation's second largest carrier, was helped by an overall improvement in the industry. The U.S. airline industry is expected to post record profits in 1996, after losing $13 billion in the first half of the decade.

Airlines benefitted from strong bookings, steady fares and extra revenues culled from the lapsed excise tax. The carriers enjoyed a windfall when the 10 percent passenger excise tax expired for eight months. The funds normally go the Federal Aviation Administration.
American, however, faces a potential strike by its pilots that has put into question the carrier's plans for a $6.5 billion airplane purchase from Boeing Co.

Crandall described 1996 as "a year in which we reaped the benefits of a favourable business environment as well as the many changes we have made over the last several years throughout the American Airlines system.

"Moreover, with the initial public offering of The Sabre Group and the announcment of our alliance with British Airways, we have laid the foundation for further progress in the years to come," he said.
Last week, American Airlines and British Airways said they formally asked the Transportation Department to approve their controversial plan to link trans-Atlantic passenger and cargo operations.

The application requested antitrust immunity for the alliance so the two carriers could coordinate their passenger and cargo services between the United States and Europe and market the services jointly.

Excluding the one-time items, the AMR earned $122 million, or $1.33 per share for the quarter. Industry analysts had on average predicted earnings of $1.25 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst estimates.
The one-time charges included a $497 million gain on AMR's initial public offering of 16 percent of The Sabre Group, the company's reservations unit.
AMR said the gain was partly offset by a $230 million after-tax charge associated with the write-down of the company's investment in troubled Canadian Airlines.
For the year, AMR had profits of $1.02 billion, or $11.19 per share, including special items. That compared with a 1995 profit of $162 million, or $2.11 a share, in 1995.
AMR took in revenues of $17.8 billion in 1996 vs. $16.9 billion in the previous year.
